title: SAP BTP: ABAP Environment (Steampunk)
excerpt: ABAP en cloud — desarrollar apps ABAP puras en BTP.
body:
## ABAP Environment
Runtime ABAP en BTP. También llamado **Steampunk** informally.

Use cases:
- Extensions S/4HANA Cloud (side-by-side)
- Nuevas apps ABAP sin server on-prem
- Migration de custom ABAP de ECC

## Provisioning
BTP cockpit → subaccount → **Instances → ABAP Environment → Create**.

Params:
- Service plan (16/32/64 users)
- Number of concurrent users
- HANA memory

## Access
### ADT (ABAP Development Tools) en Eclipse
1. Install ADT plugin
2. Add ABAP project → provide URL of the ABAP instance
3. Login con BTP creds

### Fiori launchpad para admin
URL provided por BTP cockpit.

## RAP (RESTful ABAP Programming Model)
Patrón moderno para apps CRUD:
- Data model (CDS)
- Behavior (business logic)
- Service (OData exposed)

### Ejemplo
```abap
@AccessControl.authorizationCheck: #CHECK
define root view entity ZC_Product
  as select from zproducts
{
  key product_id,
  name,
  price
}
```

Add behavior:
```abap
managed implementation in class zbp_products;

define behavior for zc_product alias Product
persistent table zproducts
lock master
{
  create; update; delete;
  field ( readonly ) product_id;
}
```

Service binding auto-generates OData v4 endpoint.

## Comunicación
### Con on-prem
Via SCC + destinations (equivalente a otras BTP apps).

### Con S/4HANA Cloud
API Business Hub — subscribe to APIs.

### Con otros BTP services
HTTP calls to destinations.

## Limitations vs ECC on-prem
- No direct DB access (queries HANA managed only)
- No custom kernel patches
- Limited native access (no OS commands)
- Auth via XSUAA (not SAP AUTH obj classic)

## Transportes
Steampunk usa **git-based** approach:
- Development en dev tenant
- Push to git → CI/CD
- Deploy to test/prod tenants

Diferente al TMS clásico.

## Users
- Login via SSO (IAS o corporate IdP)
- Roles en BTP mapped a ABAP-side auth

## Cost
Subscription-based, tiered por users + HANA size.

## Cuándo usar
- Custom logic tightly coupled con S/4HANA data
- Team ABAP existente

## Cuándo NO usar
- Modern web apps (usar CAP + Fiori)
- Data-heavy analytics (usar Datasphere)

title: SAP BTP: CAP (Cloud Application Programming Model)
excerpt: Framework SAP para construir apps enterprise (Node.js/Java).
body:
## CAP
Cloud Application Programming Model. Framework opinionated para BTP apps.

## Instalar
```bash
npm install -g @sap/cds-dk
cds init my-app
cd my-app
npm install
```

## Estructura típica
```
my-app/
  db/schema.cds        # data model
  srv/service.cds      # service definitions
  srv/service.js       # business logic
  app/                 # UI (Fiori)
  package.json
  mta.yaml             # for deployment
```

## Data model (CDS)
```cds
// db/schema.cds
namespace myapp;

entity Products {
    key ID: Integer;
    name: String(100);
    price: Decimal(10,2);
}
```

## Service (CDS)
```cds
// srv/service.cds
using { myapp } from '../db/schema';

service CatalogService {
    entity Products as projection on myapp.Products;
}
```

## Run local
```bash
cds watch
# http://localhost:4004
```

Endpoints auto-generated:
- OData v4 service
- Fiori preview UI

## Custom logic (Node.js)
```javascript
// srv/service.js
const cds = require('@sap/cds');

module.exports = (srv) => {
    srv.before('CREATE', 'Products', async (req) => {
        if (req.data.price < 0) req.reject(400, 'Price must be positive');
    });
    
    srv.on('READ', 'Products', async (req, next) => {
        const results = await next();
        // Transform results
        return results;
    });
};
```

## Deploy to BTP
```bash
mbt build
cf deploy mta_archives/my-app_1.0.0.mtar
```

## Fiori UI generation
```bash
cds add fiori-preview
# Generates a basic Fiori list-detail UI
```

Or create custom SAPUI5 app.

## Authentication
```bash
cds add xsuaa
```

Adds XSUAA integration. Users login via BTP auth.

## Database
### Local dev: SQLite (in-memory)
Default. Fast iteration.

### Prod: HANA Cloud
```bash
cds add hana
mbt build
cf deploy ...
```

Auto-migrates schema to HANA at deploy.

## OData features (out of box)
- Filtering: `?$filter=price gt 100`
- Sorting: `?$orderby=name desc`
- Paging: `?$top=10&$skip=20`
- Search: `?$search=laptop`
- Expand: `?$expand=Category`

All automatic.

## Roles + auth
```cds
service CatalogService @(requires: 'authenticated-user') {
    entity Products @(restrict: [
        { grant: 'READ', to: 'any' },
        { grant: '*', to: 'admin' }
    ]) as projection on myapp.Products;
}
```

## CAP for Java
CAP Java equivalent — Spring Boot based:
```bash
cds add java
```

For enterprise Java teams.

## Test
Unit tests con Jest / cds test:
```bash
cds add jest
npm test
```

## Docs
https://cap.cloud.sap

title: SAP BTP: SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC)
body:
## SAC
SAP Analytics Cloud — SaaS BI:
- Dashboards + reports
- Data exploration
- Planning + budgeting
- Predictive (Smart Insights, forecasting)
- Application Design

## Subscribe
BTP cockpit → **Subscriptions → SAP Analytics Cloud**.

URL: `https://<tenant>.sapanalytics.cloud`.

## Data models

### Import model
Data loaded once, refreshed periodically.

### Live model
Query real-time against source:
- HANA Cloud
- HANA on-prem (via connection)
- S/4HANA
- BW / BW4HANA
- OData

## Connect a S/4HANA
1. SAC → **Connection → New Connection**
2. Type: SAP S/4HANA (Live)
3. URL + auth
4. Test

Data queries run in source system, results shown in SAC.

## Story
Collection de visualizations (dashboard):

### Create
1. **Stories → New Story**
2. Choose blank o template
3. Add pages
4. Insert widgets:
   - Chart (bar, line, pie, etc.)
   - Table
   - KPI tile
   - Filter
   - Input control

## Analytical Application (Analytic Designer)
Code-based dashboards:
- Scripting (JavaScript-like)
- Complex logic
- Custom widgets

Más flexibility que Story.

## Planning
Budgeting, forecasting:
- Public / private versions
- What-if scenarios
- Value driver trees
- Data actions (calculations)
- Predictive scenarios (auto-forecast)

## Smart Insights
AI-powered:
- Automatic explanation of variance
- Anomaly detection
- Suggested visualizations

## Embed en apps
### Fiori launchpad
Expose SAC content en Fiori tile.

### iframe embedding
Any web app puede embed SAC story:
```html
<iframe src='https://<tenant>.sapanalytics.cloud/sap/fpa/ui/tenants/<id>/#/story?<params>'></iframe>
```

## Mobile app
SAC mobile (iOS/Android) — access stories on go.

## Users + roles
- **Viewer** — view stories
- **BI Content Creator** — build stories
- **Modeler** — data models
- **Planning content creator**
- **Admin**

Roles vía BTP subaccount.

## Cost
Per-user subscription. Multiple tiers.

## Integration con SAP Datasphere
Datasphere → SAC:
- Semantic layer in Datasphere
- SAC consumes for visualization
- Federated queries live

## Common issues
- **Data refresh failed** — source connection down
- **Slow queries** — optimize source model or use import model
- **Auth issues** — SSO / IdP config

## Alternatives
- **Power BI** — Microsoft
- **Tableau**
- **Looker** (Google)

SAC integrated tighter with SAP data sources.

title: SAP BTP: Datasphere (data warehouse cloud)
excerpt: Data warehouse managed en BTP — successor de DWC.
body:
## Datasphere
Managed data warehouse:
- Model + integrate data sources
- Business semantic layer
- Feed downstream (SAC, other tools)

Successor de Data Warehouse Cloud (DWC).

## Provision
BTP cockpit → Subscriptions → SAP Datasphere.

## Concepts

### Space
Workspace para team (dev, prod, etc.).

### Tables (physical)
Actual data storage.

### Views (virtual/materialized)
Business logic on top.

### Analytic model
Multi-dimensional model (cubes + measures).

### Perspectives
Subset views para specific consumers.

## Connect data sources

### Cloud
- S/4HANA Cloud
- SuccessFactors
- Ariba
- HANA Cloud (con other subaccount)
- Snowflake
- BigQuery

### On-prem (via SCC)
- SAP ECC
- SAP BW
- SAP HANA on-prem
- Non-SAP DB (MSSQL, Oracle, Postgres)

### Files
- CSV upload
- Excel

## Load data

### Real-time
Connection type 'live' — no data replicated, queries hit source.

### Batch
Scheduled ETL jobs — replicate to Datasphere storage.

### Streaming
From Kafka, event streams.

## Modeling

### Graphical modeler
Drag/drop UI:
- Join tables
- Transform (project, filter, aggregate)
- Create measures
- Define hierarchies

### SQL editor
Write custom SQL for advanced logic.

## Business layer
Semantic entities (business-friendly names):
- Instead of `MARA` → `Products`
- Instead of `MATNR` → `Material Number`

Self-service reporting friendly.

## Consume

### SAC
Direct connection. Access analytic models.

### External tools
OData endpoint. Tableau, PowerBI, Excel can pull.

### API
REST API para programmatic access.

## Data flows
Orchestrate ETL:
- Extract from source
- Transform (join, cleanse, enrich)
- Load to target table
- Schedule

## Governance
- Data lineage (see origin of each metric)
- Impact analysis (what breaks if I change this table?)
- Data catalog integration

## Cost
Based on:
- Data volume (storage)
- Compute (query load)
- User count

## Alternative: BW/4HANA on HANA Cloud
SAP BW/4HANA is more code-heavy (ABAP), but similar purpose. Datasphere is cloud-native successor.

title: SAP BTP: Business Application Studio (BAS)
tags: btp, bas, business application studio, ide
excerpt: IDE en cloud para dev BTP apps.
body:
## BAS
SAP Business Application Studio — Eclipse Theia-based IDE en cloud (VS Code style):
- Full-stack dev
- SAP-optimized (Fiori, CAP, ABAP)
- Preview integrations
- Deploy directo a BTP

## Provision
Subscribe en BTP cockpit → **SAP Business Application Studio**.

## Roles
Assign a users:
- **Business_Application_Studio_Developer**
- **Business_Application_Studio_Administrator**

## Access
URL: `https://<subaccount>.<region>.hana.ondemand.com` → BAS launcher.

## Dev spaces
Each user creates dev spaces:
- Type: Full Stack, SAP Fiori, SAP CAP, HANA Native, Mobile
- Extensions preselected según type

### Create
1. **Create Dev Space**
2. Nombre + type
3. Additional extensions (opcional)
4. Save

### Estados
- **Stopped**
- **Running**
- **Starting/Stopping**

## Templates para new project
BAS command palette → **Create Project from Template**:
- **SAP Fiori app** — Fiori-based UI
- **CAP project** — Node.js backend + optional UI
- **HTML5 app** — plain HTML5
- **HANA Database Module**

Generates skeleton with best practices.

## Git integration
Clone from GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket:
- SSH keys support
- HTTPS with tokens

## Deploy
One-click deploy a CF space (subaccount current).

Command palette → **Deploy MTA Archive**.

## Local dev con BAS
BAS is cloud IDE but supports:
- Local run of Node.js apps (con `npm start`)
- Preview UI en built-in browser
- Debug (breakpoints, watch variables)

## Extensions
Market:
- SAP Cloud SDK
- OData tools
- SAP HANA plugin
- Docker
- Python
- Terminal

Install from marketplace.

## Idle behavior
Dev spaces auto-stop after inactive period (~30 min).

Manual start again when needed.

## Storage
Project files persist. Dev space container has some free space (typically 8-16 GB).

Large datasets → external storage (S3 mount, etc.).

## Common issues
- **Slow performance** — dev space overloaded, restart
- **Can't connect to BTP service** — auth expired, reauth
- **Git push fails** — SSH key mismatch

## Alternatives
- **VS Code + SAP extensions** — local IDE
- **Eclipse + ADT** — for ABAP developers

BAS best for pure cloud dev flow.

title: SAP BTP: Custom Domain service
tags: btp, custom domain, dns, ssl, cname
excerpt: Serve BTP apps con your own domain (miapp.empresa.com).
body:
## Uso
Instead of default URL `myapp.cfapps.eu10.hana.ondemand.com` → `apps.empresa.com`.

Same app, own domain.

## Custom Domain service
```bash
cf create-service custom-domains standard my-domain
```

O subscription via cockpit.

## Config
1. Subaccount → Custom Domains → **New Custom Domain**
2. Enter domain (e.g., `apps.empresa.com`)
3. Configure DNS:
   - CNAME record pointing at BTP
   - Or A record if apex domain
4. Upload SSL certificate:
   - Public CA (recommended)
   - Self-signed (dev only)

### CSR generation en BTP
1. Generate CSR in Custom Domain service
2. Submit to CA (Let's Encrypt, DigiCert, etc.)
3. Get signed cert
4. Upload to Custom Domain service

## Route apps a custom domain
CF CLI:
```bash
cf create-domain my-org apps.empresa.com
cf map-route my-app apps.empresa.com -n subdomain
```

Now accessible: `https://subdomain.apps.empresa.com`.

## Wildcard cert
`*.apps.empresa.com` — covers múltiples subdomains.

One wildcard cert vs many individual certs (management ease).

## Automatic Let's Encrypt renewal
BTP soporta automatic Let's Encrypt integration:
- Enable feature
- BTP auto-renews cert every 60-90 days
- No manual intervention

## Global vs regional
Custom domain scope:
- Subaccount-level (typical)
- Region-specific (some services)

## Multi-region
Same domain apuntando diferentes regions? Complex:
- Traffic Manager (Azure) o GLB (AWS) delante
- Route users by location
- BTP subaccounts en cada region

## SEO / caching
Custom domain enables CDN:
- Cloudflare enfrente
- Serve static assets from edge
- Reduce origin load

## Common issues
- **Cert not valid** — chain missing intermediates
- **DNS not propagated** — wait 24h para propagation
- **CORS issues** — configure CORS headers explicit
- **HSTS conflict** — old cert cached por browser

## Migration
From cfapps.* to custom:
1. Setup custom domain con cert
2. Add route al app (both routes active)
3. Update marketing/links to new URL
4. Redirect old URL to new (permanent 301)
5. After grace period, remove old route

## HTTPS enforcement
By default BTP redirects HTTP → HTTPS. Custom domain honors this.

Can disable if legacy support needed (not recommended).

title: SAP BTP: Credential Store service
excerpt: Almacenar y rotar secretos con Credential Store service.
body:
## Uso
Secrets management managed:
- API keys de external services
- Passwords de systems on-prem
- Encryption keys

Secrets stored encrypted, retrievable at runtime.

## Create service
```bash
cf create-service credstore free my-credstore
cf bind-service my-app my-credstore
```

## Add credentials
BTP cockpit → Credential Store → Instance → **Credentials**:

### Password (single string)
- Name: `smtp-password`
- Value: `MyPass123`
- Description

### Key (JSON)
- Name: `api-key`
- Value: `{"key": "...", "secret": "..."}`

### Certificate (X.509)
- Upload cert + private key

## Retrieve from app
```javascript
const credstore = require('@sap-cloud-sdk/credential-store');

const pass = await credstore.readCredentials({
    namespace: 'default',
    name: 'smtp-password'
});

const smtpPassword = pass.value;
```

## Namespaces
Multiple namespaces para isolation:
- `prod`
- `dev`
- `team-a`

Apps con permission solo a their namespace.

## Rotation
Manual:
1. Update credential value en cockpit
2. Apps auto-fetch new value en next call (or cache expiry)

Automated (external): script updates via API.

## Encryption at rest
All credentials encrypted via BTP's KMS. Never stored en cleartext.

## API access
```bash
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $token' \
     https://credstore-endpoint/api/v1/credentials/default/smtp-password
```

Requires XSUAA token.

## Audit
All credential access logged. Compliance-ready.

## Common issues
- **'Credential not found'** — namespace o name typo
- **'Access denied'** — app not bound to correct instance
- **'Instance not accessible'** — creds instance en other subaccount

## Alternative
- **Env vars** — simpler but less secure
- **HashiCorp Vault** — for hybrid setups

Credential Store BTP-native, integrated OAuth.

title: SAP BTP: Object Store service
tags: btp, object store, s3, azure blob, storage
body:
## Object Store
Managed S3-compatible storage:
- Store files (docs, images, backups)
- API S3
- Backed by AWS S3, Azure Blob, GCP Storage según region

## Create
```bash
cf create-service objectstore standard my-storage
cf bind-service my-app my-storage
```

## Access
App reads credentials via VCAP_SERVICES:
```javascript
const vcap = JSON.parse(process.env.VCAP_SERVICES);
const creds = vcap.objectstore[0].credentials;

// AWS SDK
const AWS = require('aws-sdk');
const s3 = new AWS.S3({
    accessKeyId: creds.access_key_id,
    secretAccessKey: creds.secret_access_key,
    endpoint: creds.host,
    region: creds.region
});

const bucket = creds.bucket;
```

## Common operations
### Upload
```javascript
await s3.putObject({
    Bucket: bucket,
    Key: 'reports/2026-07/report.pdf',
    Body: fileBuffer,
    ContentType: 'application/pdf'
}).promise();
```

### Download
```javascript
const obj = await s3.getObject({
    Bucket: bucket,
    Key: 'reports/2026-07/report.pdf'
}).promise();
res.send(obj.Body);
```

### List
```javascript
const list = await s3.listObjectsV2({
    Bucket: bucket,
    Prefix: 'reports/'
}).promise();
```

### Delete
```javascript
await s3.deleteObject({
    Bucket: bucket,
    Key: 'reports/old.pdf'
}).promise();
```

## Presigned URLs
Generate URL for temporary access (download without exposing credentials):
```javascript
const url = s3.getSignedUrl('getObject', {
    Bucket: bucket,
    Key: 'report.pdf',
    Expires: 3600  // 1 hour
});
// Share URL con user
```

## Multi-tenant
Multiple apps can share instance con different key prefixes:
- App A: `app-a/files/...`
- App B: `app-b/files/...`

O create instance per app.

## Lifecycle policies
Auto-delete after N days, o archive to cold storage:
Configured via S3 API o BTP cockpit (limited UI).

## Encryption
At rest (server-side encryption) automatic.
In transit HTTPS.

## Cost
- Storage: per GB/month
- Requests: per 1000
- Data transfer (egress)

Enable **intelligent tiering** if data access varies.

## Backup
Managed. Point-in-time restore available.

## Common issues
- **AccessDenied** — check IAM roles
- **NoSuchBucket** — instance not properly provisioned
- **SlowUpload** — use multipart upload for >100 MB files

title: SAP BTP: HTML5 Application Repository
body:
## Uso
HTML5 Application Repository = storage + serving de UI5 apps y assets estáticos.

Distinto de un app CF (con backend Node.js). Es solo frontend static.

## Componentes

### App Router
Handles auth + routing. Deployed as CF app.

### HTML5 Repository
Storage de app files (uploaded once, served many times).

### Portal service o Launchpad Service
Aggregates apps en launchpad.

## Deploy Fiori app

### Prerequisites
- MTA con html5 module
- xsuaa instance
- destination service (opcional)

### mta.yaml example
```yaml
ID: fiori-app
version: 1.0.0
modules:
  - name: approuter
    type: approuter.nodejs
    path: approuter
    requires:
      - name: xsuaa-service
      - name: html5-repo-runtime
  - name: ui
    type: html5
    path: ui
    build-parameters:
      builder: custom
      commands:
        - npm install
        - npm run build
      supported-platforms: []
resources:
  - name: xsuaa-service
    type: org.cloudfoundry.managed-service
    parameters:
      service: xsuaa
      service-plan: application
  - name: html5-repo-runtime
    type: org.cloudfoundry.managed-service
    parameters:
      service: html5-apps-repo
      service-plan: app-runtime
  - name: html5-repo-host
    type: org.cloudfoundry.managed-service
    parameters:
      service: html5-apps-repo
      service-plan: app-host
```

### Build + deploy
```bash
mbt build
cf deploy mta_archives/fiori-app_1.0.0.mtar
```

## Access
URL: `https://<approuter-route>.cfapps.eu10.hana.ondemand.com/<app-path>`

## Launchpad
BTP Work Zone (formerly Launchpad Service):
- Aggregate multiple apps
- Central navigation
- Customizable themes

### Launchpad admin
BTP cockpit → Launchpad → **Site**:
- Create site
- Add apps (from HTML5 repo)
- Group into tiles
- Assign to roles

## Users see launchpad
`https://<launchpad>.cfapps.eu10.hana.ondemand.com`

Auth via XSUAA (SSO).

## Versioning
Upload multiple versions. Users see latest by default.

Rollback: delete/downgrade version.

## Cache
HTML5 apps cached en browser + CDN. Deploy new version → busts cache via ETags.

## Common issues
- **404** — app not deployed to repo
- **Auth loop** — approuter misconfig, check xs-app.json routing
- **UI5 not loading** — SAPUI5 library version mismatch
- **CORS on destination call** — configure CORS in destination

title: SAP BTP: SAP Cloud Integration (CPI)
tags: btp, cpi, integration suite, iflow, esb
excerpt: Servicio de integración (ex-HCI) para conectar sistemas.
body:
## Cloud Integration (CPI)
Parte de SAP Integration Suite. Successor de SAP PI/PO on-prem.

ESB en cloud:
- Message transformation
- Content-based routing
- Multiple protocols

## Provisioning
Subscribe en BTP cockpit → **Integration Suite → Cloud Integration**.

## Access
URL: `https://<tenant>.integrationsuite.cfapps.eu10.hana.ondemand.com`

## Concepts
### iFlow (Integration Flow)
Graphical flow: sender → processors → receiver.

### Adapters
- HTTP
- SFTP
- Mail
- OData
- IDoc
- REST
- SOAP
- JMS
- Kafka

### Message Mapping
Transform XML/JSON structure.

### Content Modifier
Change headers, properties, body.

### Router
Content-based routing (if/else).

### Splitter / Gather
Process in parallel, aggregate results.

## Create iFlow
1. Integration Suite → **Design → Integration Package → New**
2. Package name
3. Add **Integration Flow**
4. Design UI: drag components
5. Configure
6. Save + Deploy

## Ejemplo simple
```
[HTTP Sender] → [Content Modifier: set headers] → [Message Mapping: JSON to XML] → [HTTP Receiver: send to SAP ECC]
```

## Deploy iFlow
Save → Deploy button. Assigns endpoint URL.

## Ver monitoring
Operations → **Monitor Message Processing**:
- Filter por iFlow, time range, status
- Successful / failed messages
- Payload inspection
- Retry

## Value mappings
Static lookups (customer ID cross-reference).

## Groovy scripting
Custom logic embedded:
```groovy
def Message processData(Message message) {
    def body = message.getBody(String)
    // Transform
    message.setBody(body.toUpperCase())
    return message
}
```

## Security
### Sender auth
- Basic auth
- OAuth
- Client cert

### Receiver auth
- Configured en credentials store

## Credentials
BTP Integration Suite credentials — encrypted storage.

## Certificates
Manage TLS certs y user X.509 en **Manage Security Material**.

## Testing
- **Simulate iFlow** con sample payload
- Actual invoke con curl / Postman

## Deploy environments
- Dev tenant
- Test tenant
- Prod tenant

Transport packages between via **CTS+** o manual export/import.

## Migration from PI/PO
SAP provides migration tools. Not automated 100%.

## Cost
Based on messages per month + connections.

title: SAP BTP: SAP API Management
excerpt: API gateway para exposé, protect, monetize APIs.
body:
## API Management
Part of SAP Integration Suite.

## Use cases
- Publish backend APIs con transformations
- Rate limiting + throttling
- Authentication + authorization
- Analytics de usage
- API monetization (paid tiers)

## Provisioning
BTP cockpit → **Integration Suite → API Management** → activate.

## Access
URL del portal API Management.

## Concepts

### API Provider
Source system (backend). Ejemplo: S/4HANA con OData services.

### API Proxy
Facade en API Mgmt que fronts the backend. Puede tener policies.

### API Product
Bundle of API proxies. Consumers subscribe.

### Consumer app
External app que consumes APIs.

## Create API proxy
1. **API Portal → APIs → Create**
2. **API Provider** o **URL** del backend
3. Import OpenAPI spec (if available)
4. Save

## Policies
Apply behavior en request/response:

### Rate limit
Max N calls per minute per app.

### Quota
Max N calls per month.

### Auth
Require API key, OAuth, JWT.

### Transformation
JSON to XML, add/remove headers.

### Threat protection
- SQL injection detection
- JSON bomb protection
- Rate limiting DDoS

### CORS
Allow cross-origin.

### Logging
Custom analytics events.

## Deploy proxy
After policies configured → deploy → API accessible en API Mgmt URL.

## Consumer registration
### Developer Portal
Self-service portal for API consumers:
- Register app
- Get API key
- Subscribe to products

### API keys
Consumer gets unique key. Include en requests:
```
GET /api/products
APIKey: xxx
```

API Mgmt verifies key → applies quota + rate limits.

## Analytics
OOB dashboards:
- API usage per consumer
- Error rates
- Latency
- Geographic distribution

## Monetization (paid tiers)
User plans:
- **Free** — 1000 calls/month
- **Basic** — 10000 calls/month, $10/mo
- **Premium** — unlimited, $100/mo

Billing integration optional.

## Deploy multi-env
- Dev tenant → build
- Test tenant → validate
- Prod tenant → serve consumers

## Common issues
- **429 Too Many Requests** — quota exceeded
- **401 Unauthorized** — API key invalid or missing
- **502 Bad Gateway** — backend unreachable
- **Slow response** — backend slow, o policy overhead

## Best practices
- **Rate limit** siempre — protect backend
- **API versioning** — `/v1/`, `/v2/`
- **Deprecation warnings** — informar consumers antes de sunset
- **OpenAPI spec** — machine-readable docs

title: SAP BTP: SAP Signavio Process Insights
excerpt: Process mining para SAP: detectar bottlenecks reales.
body:
## Signavio Process Insights
SaaS de process mining en BTP:
- Consume real logs de S/4HANA / ECC
- Reconstruct process end-to-end
- Detect variants, bottlenecks, deviations

## Setup
1. Subscribe en BTP
2. Configure data extraction from source SAP system (agent installed on-prem)
3. Signavio ingests + analyzes
4. Dashboards + insights

## Extraction
Ejemplo Order-to-Cash:
- Sales order create
- Delivery create
- Goods issue
- Invoice create
- Payment received

Each event timestamped → process timeline.

## Insights

### Process map
Visualize actual flow, not idealized.

### Bottleneck detection
Which steps take longest?

### Variant analysis
How many paths exist? Are some inefficient?

### Deviation detection
Unusual sequences (skipped steps, reworks).

### Root cause analysis
By attribute (region, customer, product) → why deviations happen.

## KPIs
OOB metrics:
- Cycle time
- Throughput
- Rework rate
- On-time delivery

## Business context
Combines process data con business impact:
- Financial (cost of delay)
- Operational (# affected orders)

## Recommendations
AI suggests improvements:
- Automate specific steps
- Adjust SLA thresholds
- Reallocate resources

## Integration with SAP Build Process Automation
Detect issue in Signavio → automate fix con Build Process Automation.

## Sample use cases

### Late payments
Analyze A/R aging processes → identify why some customers pay late (approvals stuck, wrong contact).

### Production delays
Production order variance → identify machine downtime patterns.

### Purchase-to-Pay inefficiencies
Why some invoices posted late? Approvals slow? Data quality?

## Data privacy
Common concern:
- Personal data en logs?
- Anonymize where possible
- GDPR/LGPD compliance

## Cost
Subscription + data volume tiered.

## Alternatives
- **Celonis** — market leader (SAP is customer + partner)
- **UiPath Process Mining**
- Custom analytics con BW / SAC

title: SAP BTP: consumo de S/4HANA APIs via API Business Hub
excerpt: Descubrir + consumir APIs SAP via SAP API Business Hub.
body:
## API Business Hub
Central catalog de todas las APIs SAP:
- S/4HANA (Cloud + on-prem)
- SuccessFactors
- Ariba
- Concur
- IntegrationSuite adapters

URL: https://api.sap.com

## Uso

### Discover
Search por keyword, category, product.

### Try en sandbox
Each API tiene sandbox environment:
- Test calls con dummy data
- Sin credentials propias
- Learn API before consuming en real

### Get details
- OpenAPI spec
- Documentation
- Payload examples
- Auth requirements

## Consuming from BTP app

### Method 1: Direct HTTPS
App calls the API endpoint con OAuth 2.0 token.

### Method 2: SAP Cloud SDK
```bash
npm install @sap-cloud-sdk/http-client
```

```javascript
const { executeHttpRequest } = require('@sap-cloud-sdk/http-client');

const response = await executeHttpRequest(
    { destinationName: 'S4HANA_DEST' },
    { method: 'get', url: '/API_BUSINESS_PARTNER/A_BusinessPartner' }
);
```

### Method 3: OData v4 client generation
Generate typed client from OData metadata:
```bash
npx @sap-cloud-sdk/generator -i ./metadata -o ./client
```

Type-safe client:
```javascript
const { businessPartnerService } = require('./client');
const partners = await businessPartnerService.getAllBusinessPartner().execute({ destinationName: 'S4HANA_DEST' });
```

## Auth para S/4HANA Cloud APIs
- OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials
- App registered en S/4HANA Cloud → get client ID + secret
- Configure en BTP destination

## Auth para S/4HANA on-prem APIs
- Via SCC tunnel
- User authentication with principal propagation, o technical user
- OAuth 2.0 also supported if configured

## API rate limits
Each API has its own limits. Check documentation.

S/4HANA Cloud typical: 100k calls/day per app.

## Common APIs

### API_BUSINESS_PARTNER
- Customers, vendors, employees
- CRUD operations

### API_PRODUCT
- Material master
- Product hierarchy

### API_SALES_ORDER
- Create/read/update sales orders
- Get status

### API_PURCHASEORDER_PROCESS
- Purchase orders CRUD

### API_JOURNALENTRY_SRV
- Post journal entries a FI

## Sandbox vs Production
- Sandbox: sap.com/business-accelerator-hub (test data, no persist)
- Production: your S/4HANA tenant

Don't test destructive ops en production!

## Custom APIs
Expose custom APIs from ABAP:
- ABAP CDS + service binding
- Register en API Hub (optional)

## Governance
- Track APIs consumed
- Version awareness (deprecations)
- Update code before EOL

title: SAP BTP: monitoring y observability
excerpt: Herramientas nativas + externas para monitor BTP apps.
body:
## Native BTP monitoring

### App metrics
CF app: `cf app my-app` → CPU, memory, instances.

BTP cockpit → app → **Runtime** — metrics visualizados.

### Application Logs service
Kibana dashboards — search + visualize logs.

### Cloud Foundry monitoring plugin
```bash
cf install-plugin monitoring
cf monitoring
```

## Application Autoscaler
Auto-scale CF apps based on metrics:

```bash
cf create-service autoscaler standard my-autoscaler
cf bind-service my-app my-autoscaler
```

Rules:
- Scale up if CPU > 80% for 5 min
- Scale down if CPU < 30% for 10 min

### Manifest attach
```yaml
applications:
  - name: my-app
    services:
      - my-autoscaler
    env:
      AUTOSCALE_INSTANCES_MIN: 2
      AUTOSCALE_INSTANCES_MAX: 10
```

## Third-party integration

### Splunk
Install Splunk Forwarder en app o forward via syslog.

### Datadog
Datadog agent runs alongside app, sends metrics/logs to Datadog cloud.

### New Relic
APM (Application Performance Monitoring):
- Node.js/Java agent embedded
- Trace requests end-to-end
- Detect slow queries, errors

## Distributed tracing
### OpenTelemetry
Standard for distributed tracing.

```bash
npm install @opentelemetry/api @opentelemetry/sdk-node
```

```javascript
const opentelemetry = require('@opentelemetry/sdk-node');
// Configure exporter to Jaeger/Zipkin
```

### Trace visualization
- Jaeger UI
- Zipkin
- SAP Cloud ALM (if subscribed)

## Alertas

### Alert Notification service
Cubierto en artículo separado.

### Sample alerts
- Error rate > 5%
- P99 latency > 2 sec
- Memory usage > 90%
- App instance count = 0 (all down!)

## Health endpoints
Expose `/health` en app:
```javascript
app.get('/health', (req, res) => {
    res.json({
        status: 'ok',
        uptime: process.uptime(),
        timestamp: new Date().toISOString()
    });
});
```

CF healthcheck config:
```yaml
applications:
  - name: my-app
    health-check-type: http
    health-check-http-endpoint: /health
```

Unhealthy → CF restarts app.

## SAP Cloud ALM
Enterprise-level ALM:
- Monitoring, incident management, ITSM
- Cross-landscape (SAP + BTP + on-prem)
- Central dashboard

Requires SAP Support subscription.

## SLO / SLA tracking
Define SLOs (Service Level Objectives):
- Availability: 99.9%
- Latency p99: <500 ms
- Error rate: <1%

Measure con dashboards. Report to stakeholders.

## Cost monitoring
BTP cockpit → **Cost → Consumption**:
- Per subaccount, per service
- Trend over time
- Alert on cost spike

## Best practices
- **Structured logs** (JSON)
- **Correlation IDs** for tracing
- **Health endpoints** on all apps
- **Autoscaler** for variable load
- **Alerts** para critical failures
- **Dashboards** shared con team + stakeholders

title: SAP BTP: cost management y consumption
excerpt: Monitorear y optimizar costos en BTP.
body:
## Consumption model

### Subscription
Fixed price per service (SaaS): Analytics Cloud, IAS, etc.

### CPEA (Consumption Pattern for Enterprise Agreements)
Cloud credits pre-purchased → consumed pay-as-you-go:
- Compute (CF instance-hours)
- Storage (HANA GB)
- API calls
- Data volume

## Ver consumption
BTP cockpit → global account → **Costs and Usage**:
- Total spend
- Per subaccount
- Per service
- Trend graphs

## Detailed breakdown
Export CSV con line items:
- Timestamp
- Service
- Metric (e.g., CPU-hours)
- Amount

## Budget alerts
Set budget:
- Monthly limit
- Alert at 50%, 75%, 90%
- Recipients (finance + tech leads)

## Optimize compute
### Right-size CF apps
- Don't over-allocate memory (default 128M, only increase if needed)
- Fewer instances if load allows

### Autoscaler
Scale down during off-hours automatically.

### Stop non-prod at night/weekends
Dev/test envs no need 24/7:
- Cron job: `cf stop my-app` at 8 PM Fri
- `cf start` at 8 AM Mon

## Optimize HANA Cloud
- Right-size tier
- Auto-stop dev instances
- Compression settings
- Archive cold data to cheaper tier

## Optimize storage
- Object Store: lifecycle rules (move old to Glacier-equivalent)
- Logs: retention shorter en dev

## Optimize services
### Consolidate
Multiple `xsuaa` instances → consolidate donde posible.

### Downgrade plans
- Application Logs: standard vs lite
- Feature Flags: lite may suffice

## Free tier
Many services have free tiers para dev/test:
- Use free plan for non-prod
- Reserve paid plans for prod

## Cost per subaccount
Assign cost centers to subaccounts. Chargeback en enterprise:
- Finance dept → their subaccount cost
- IT dept → theirs

Use tags/descriptions.

## Common pitfalls

### Forgotten resources
- Old app instances still running
- Test databases not deleted
- Old versions of services

**Regular cleanup**: quarterly audit.

### Over-provisioned
Memory much higher than actual usage. Reduce.

### Non-prod full-scale
Dev has 8 GB HANA when 4 GB suffices.

### Egress
Data transfer out of BTP region: costs $$. Watch.

## Reserved capacity
Commit para year → discount (~30-40%). Good for stable workloads.

Negotiate con SAP account manager.

## Cost reports for management
- Monthly summary email
- Cost per business unit
- YoY comparison
- Projections vs budget

## BTP Cost Reporting API
Programmatic access:
```bash
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
     https://accountsservice.cfapps.eu10.hana.ondemand.com/api/v1/globalAccounts/<id>/consumption
```

Build custom dashboards.

## Trial subaccount
SAP offers trial: 90-day free access. Convert to paid seamlessly.

## Tips
- Estimate before deploy (BTP cost calculator online)
- Review monthly
- Optimize continuously
- Educate team on cost implications
